request.query: In a locally finite ordered Finsupp space the cardinality of a finite set bounded above by f is at most product of cardinalities of Iic(f i) over support

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Iic(f) Equals Product of Iic(f(i)) over Support
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] [inst_2 : CanonicallyOrderedAdd α]
  [inst_3 : OrderBot α] [inst_4 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : DecidableEq α] (f : ι →₀ α),
  (Finset.Iic f).card = ∏ i ∈ f.support, (Finset.Iic (f i)).card
items.informal_description: For a finite support function $ f $, the cardinality of the set $ \{x \mid x \le f\} $ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of $ \{y \mid y \le f(i)\} $ for each $ i $ in the support of $ f $. In symbols, $ \#(\text{Iic}(f)) = \prod_{i \in \text{support}(f)} \#(\text{Iic}(f(i))) $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of $[0, f]$ in DFinsupp Equals Product Over Support
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)]
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (α i)] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (α i)]
  [inst_4 : ∀ (i : ι), CanonicallyOrderedAdd (α i)] [inst_5 : (i : ι) → OrderBot (α i)]
  [inst_6 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)] (f : Π₀ (i : ι), α i),
  (Finset.Iic f).card = ∏ i ∈ f.support, (Finset.Iic (f i)).card
items.informal_description:
The cardinality of the interval $[0, f]$ in the type of dependent finite support functions is equal to the product of the cardinalities of the intervals $[0, f(i)]$ for each index $i$ in the support of $f$. Here, $0$ denotes the zero function (the bottom element), and the support of $f$ consists of indices where $f(i) 
eq 0$.

items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] [inst_2 : CanonicallyOrderedAdd α]
  [inst_3 : OrderBot α] [inst_4 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : DecidableEq α] (f : ι →₀ α),
  (Finset.Iio f).card = ∏ i ∈ f.support, (Finset.Iic (f i)).card - 1
items.informal_description: For a finite support function $ f $, the cardinality of the set $ \{x \mid x < f\} $ (denoted $ \mathrm{Iio}(f) $) is equal to the product over all $ i $ in the support of $ f $ of $ (\#\mathrm{Iic}(f(i)) - 1) $, where $ \mathrm{Iic}(f(i)) $ denotes the finite set $ \{y \mid y \leq f(i)\} $.

  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (α i)] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (α i)]
  [inst_4 : ∀ (i : ι), CanonicallyOrderedAdd (α i)] [inst_5 : (i : ι) → OrderBot (α i)]

items.informal_description: For a dependent finite support function $ f $ with values in a family of locally finite ordered types with bottom elements, the cardinality of the set $ \{x \mid x < f\} $ equals $ \left(\prod_{i \in \text{supp}(f)} \#\{y \mid y \leq f(i)\} \right) - 1 $, where $ \text{supp}(f) $ denotes the finite support of $ f $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Unordered Interval Between Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : Lattice α] [inst_1 : Zero α] [inst_2 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] (f g : ι →₀ α),
  (Finset.uIcc f g).card = ∏ i ∈ f.support ∪ g.support, (Finset.uIcc (f i) (g i)).card
items.informal_description: For finite support functions $f, g : \iota \to_0 \alpha$ where $\alpha$ is a locally finite ordered lattice, the cardinality of the unordered interval $[f, g]$ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of the intervals $[f(i), g(i)]$ for all $i$ in the union of the supports of $f$ and $g$. Formally, $\#(\mathrm{uIcc}\, f\, g) = \prod_{i \in \mathrm{support}\, f \cup \mathrm{support}\, g} \#(\mathrm{uIcc}\, (f(i))\, (g(i)))$.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Unordered Interval in Dependent Finite Support Functions as Product Over Supports
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)]
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Lattice (α i)] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → Zero (α i)] [inst_4 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)]
  (f g : Π₀ (i : ι), α i), (Finset.uIcc f g).card = ∏ i ∈ f.support ∪ g.support, (Finset.uIcc (f i) (g i)).card
items.informal_description: For two dependent finite support functions $ f $ and $ g $ with values in a family of locally finite ordered types $ \{\alpha_i\} $, the cardinality of the unordered interval $[f, g]$ equals the product of the cardinalities of the componentwise intervals $[f(i), g(i)]$ over all indices $ i $ in the union of their supports. Formally, $ |[f, g]| = \prod_{i \in \text{supp}(f) \cup \text{supp}(g)} |[f(i), g(i)]| $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Interval in Dependent Finite Support Functions Equals Product of Component Intervals
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)]
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (α i)] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → Zero (α i)] [inst_4 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)]
  (f g : Π₀ (i : ι), α i), (Finset.Icc f g).card = ∏ i ∈ f.support ∪ g.support, (Finset.Icc (f i) (g i)).card
items.informal_description: For two dependent finite support functions $ f $ and $ g $, the cardinality of the closed interval $[f, g]$ (under the pointwise order) is equal to the product of the cardinalities of the intervals $[f(i), g(i)]$ for each index $ i $ in the union of the supports of $ f $ and $ g $. This holds because each target type $ \alpha(i) $ is locally finite, ensuring each component interval is finite, and the union of supports is finite.
